records.literal_gloss: I love, because YHWH hears my voice, my pleas.

en.L: I love [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hears my voice, my pleas.
en.B: I love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listens when I call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and plead for mercy.
en.R: I love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears me when I pray and ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for help.

decisions.choice: I love: the object is left unspoken
alternatives: I love it that the LORD hears
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. The sense is that the psalmist loves the LORD because he heard; it may also mean "I am glad that the LORD hears".

decisions.choice: pleas: cries for mercy
decisions.reason: The word (tachanunim) is a plea for grace or favor (28:2; 86:6).

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the object of "love" (m1); Literal brackets it.

records.literal_gloss: For he has turned his ear to me, and in my days I will call.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ear to me, and in my days I will call.
en.B: Because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ear toward me, I will call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all my days.
en.R: He bends down to listen to me, so I will pray to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} every day of my life.

decisions.choice: turned his ear: listened closely
decisions.reason: To turn or bend the ear is to lean in and listen (17:6; 31:3).

decisions.choice: in my days: as long as I live
decisions.reason: "My days" are the days of his life.

decisions.choice: to him (B); pray to him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the one he will call to.

source.text: אֲפָפ֤וּנִי׀חֶבְלֵי־מָ֗וֶת וּמְצָרֵ֣י שְׁא֣וֹל מְצָא֑וּנִי צָרָ֖ה וְיָג֣וֹן אֶמְצָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Encircled me [the] cords of death, and [the] distresses of Sheol found me; trouble and sorrow I found.

en.L: The cords of death surrounded me, and the distresses of Sheol found me; trouble and sorrow I found.
en.B: The ropes of death were wound around me, and the anguish of Sheol had caught me; I met with distress and grief.
en.R: It was as if death had tied me up with ropes. I was afraid I would soon be in the place of the dead. I was full of trouble and sorrow.

decisions.choice: the cords of death: as in 18:5-6
decisions.reason: The same picture of death as a hunter's ropes appears in 18:5-6. The word (chevel) can mean cords or birth pangs.

decisions.choice: distresses of Sheol: the grip of the grave
decisions.reason: The word (metsarim) is a narrow, tight place; Sheol is the place of the dead (6:6). The psalmist was near death.

decisions.choice: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable explains Sheol.

source.text: וּבְשֵֽׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֶקְרָ֑א אָנָּ֥ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה מַלְּטָ֥ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And on [the] name of YHWH I called: Please, YHWH, rescue my soul!

en.L: And on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I called: Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, rescue my soul!
en.B: So I cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by name: Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save my life!
en.R: So I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please save my life!

decisions.choice: call on the name of the LORD: pray to him
decisions.reason: To call on his name is to pray to the LORD as the God who has made himself known (Genesis 12:8; verses 13 and 17).

decisions.choice: please: an urgent plea
decisions.reason: The word ('anna) is a strong "please!", used in desperate prayer (118:25).

decisions.choice: soul: life
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the self or life (3:3).

decisions.choice: my life
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, nefesh is "my life" where the danger is death.

records.literal_gloss: Gracious [is] YHWH and righteous, and our God [is] compassionate.

en.L: Gracious [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and righteous; and our God [is] compassionate.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} shows grace and does what is right; our God is tender and merciful.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is kind and always does what is right. Our God shows mercy.

decisions.choice: gracious and compassionate: Exodus 34:6
decisions.reason: As in 111:4, the words recall the LORD's description of himself to Moses.

decisions.choice: righteous: he does what is right
decisions.reason: The LORD is righteous (tsaddiq) in that he acts rightly and keeps faith, here by saving the one who called.

source.text: שֹׁמֵ֣ר פְּתָאיִ֣ם יְהֹוָ֑ה דַּ֝לּוֹתִ֗י וְלִ֣י יְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Guarding [the] simple [is] YHWH; I was brought low, and to me he gave salvation.

en.L: Guarding the simple [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I was brought low, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved me.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} keeps watch over people with no defense; when I sank down helpless, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued me.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} protects people who cannot protect themselves. When I was weak and helpless, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved me.

decisions.choice: the simple: people with no cunning or defense
decisions.reason: The word (peta'im) can mean the foolish (Proverbs 1:22), but here, as in 19:8, it is the open and unprotected, who cannot help themselves.

decisions.choice: I was brought low: weak, at the end of my strength
decisions.reason: The verb (dalal) is to be low or thin, weakened (79:8; 142:7).

decisions.choice: people with no defense (B); people who cannot protect themselves (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the word here (m1).

source.text: שׁוּבִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי לִמְנוּחָ֑יְכִי כִּֽי־יְ֝הוָ֗ה גָּמַ֥ל עָלָֽיְכִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Return, my soul, to your rest, for YHWH has dealt fully with you.

en.L: Return, my soul, to your rest, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has dealt bountifully with you.
en.B: Come back to your rest, my soul, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has treated you with kindness.
en.R: I can rest and be calm again, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been so good to me.

decisions.choice: Return, my soul: the psalmist speaks to himself
decisions.reason: As in 42:6 and 103:1, he addresses his own soul, calling himself back to peace.

decisions.choice: dealt bountifully: done good in full measure
decisions.reason: The verb (gamal) is to deal out fully, here in kindness (13:6; 142:8).

decisions.choice: I can rest
decisions.reason: Readable turns the self-address into a plain statement (m1).

source.text: כִּ֤י חִלַּ֥צְתָּ נַפְשִׁ֗י מִ֫מָּ֥וֶת אֶת־עֵינִ֥י מִן־דִּמְעָ֑ה אֶת־רַגְלִ֥י מִדֶּֽחִי׃

records.literal_gloss: For you have rescued my soul from death, my eye from tears, my foot from stumbling.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have rescued my soul from death, my eye from tears, my foot from stumbling.
en.B: You have pulled me back from death, kept my eyes from weeping and my feet from tripping.
en.R: You saved me from dying. You dried my tears and kept me from falling.

decisions.choice: you: the psalmist turns to speak to God
decisions.reason: After speaking of the LORD (verses 5-7), he now addresses him directly.

decisions.choice: close to 56:14
decisions.reason: 56:14 has nearly the same words: "you have rescued my soul from death, my feet from stumbling".

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: As in 116:4, nefesh is the person's life.

records.literal_gloss: I will walk before YHWH in [the] lands of the living.

en.L: I will walk before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the lands of the living.
en.B: I will go about my life in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, here in the lands of the living.
en.R: I will go on living, and I will spend my days in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: walk before the LORD: live in his presence and service
decisions.reason: To walk before someone is to live under his eye and in his service (Genesis 17:1; 56:14).

decisions.choice: the lands of the living: this life
decisions.reason: The phrase is the world of the living as against the place of the dead (27:13; Isaiah 38:11).

source.text: הֶ֭אֱמַנְתִּי כִּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אֲ֝נִ֗י עָנִ֥יתִי מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: I believed, for I spoke: I, I am greatly afflicted.

en.L: I believed, even when I said, I am greatly afflicted.
en.B: I kept my faith even when I said, I am suffering terribly.
en.R: I kept on trusting, even when I said, My suffering is terrible.

decisions.choice: I believed, even when I spoke
decisions.reason: The joining word (ki) is hard here. It most likely means "even when": he trusted even while he said how afflicted he was. It may also mean "for" or "therefore".

decisions.choice: quoted in 2 Corinthians 4:13
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the ancient Greek translation, "I believed, therefore I spoke", for his own preaching in the middle of suffering.

decisions.choice: believed: trusted, held firm
decisions.reason: The verb (he'emin) is to trust, to be firm in relying on someone (78:22).

records.literal_gloss: I, I said in my alarm: Every human [is] a liar.

en.L: I said in my alarm, every human [is] a liar.
en.B: In my panic I said, Every human being is false.
en.R: When I was terrified, I said, No one can be trusted!

decisions.choice: alarm: panic, hurried fear
decisions.reason: The verb (chafaz) is to hurry away in fear (31:23).

decisions.choice: liar: one who fails you
decisions.reason: The word (kozev) is a liar, and also something that disappoints, like a stream that runs dry. In his terror he found that no human help could be relied on; only the LORD could. Romans 3:4 echoes the Greek of this line.

decisions.choice: No one can be trusted
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the saying (m2).

records.literal_gloss: What will I return to YHWH, all his benefits [are] on me?

en.L: What shall I give back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [for] all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} benefits to me?
en.B: What return can I make to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kindness to me?
en.R: What can I give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for all the good things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for me?

decisions.choice: benefits: good deeds done for me
decisions.reason: The word (tagmul) is from the verb of verse 7 (gamal): what the LORD has dealt out to him in kindness.

decisions.choice: What will I return: an answer follows
decisions.reason: The question is answered in verses 13-14: he cannot repay, but he can give thanks publicly and keep his vows.

records.literal_gloss: [The] cup of salvations I will lift up, and on [the] name of YHWH I will call.

en.L: The cup of salvation I will lift up, and on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will call.
en.B: I will lift high the cup of salvation and call out the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will lift up a cup to thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for saving me, and I will call on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name in prayer.

decisions.choice: the cup of salvation: a cup raised in thanks
decisions.reason: The cup was probably raised and drunk, or poured out, with the thank offering of verse 17 (Numbers 28:7 speaks of drink offerings). "Salvations" is plural: full rescue.

decisions.choice: a cup to thank the LORD for saving me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup is for (m1).

records.literal_gloss: My vows to YHWH I will pay, before, please, all his people.

en.L: My vows to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will pay, [yes], in the presence of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.
en.B: What I promised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will carry out, with all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people looking on.
en.R: I will do what I promised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people will see me do it.

decisions.choice: vows: promises made in trouble, kept with an offering
decisions.reason: In danger people promised God an offering if he rescued them (66:13-14; Leviticus 7:16). Keeping the vow publicly, before all his people, was part of giving thanks.

decisions.choice: please: a particle of emphasis
decisions.reason: The small word (na') usually means "please"; here it gives emphasis.

records.literal_gloss: Precious in [the] eyes of YHWH [is] the death of his faithful ones.

en.L: Precious in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] the death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful ones.
en.B: The death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal ones weighs heavily in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does not let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful people die lightly. Their lives are precious to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: precious: costly, of great worth
alternatives: the death of his faithful ones is a grievous thing to him
decisions.reason: The word (yaqar) is costly, valuable. The LORD does not let the death of his own happen lightly; their blood is precious in his sight (72:14). It does not say he is pleased by their death.

decisions.choice: faithful ones: those bound to him in loyal love
decisions.reason: The word (chasidim) is from chesed: people who are loyal to the LORD (4:4; 30:5).

decisions.choice: weighs heavily (B); does not let ... lightly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of the word here (m1).

source.text: אָֽנָּ֣ה יְהוָה֮ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֪י עַ֫בְדֶּ֥ךָ אֲֽנִי־עַ֭בְדְּךָ בֶּן־אֲמָתֶ֑ךָ פִּ֝תַּ֗חְתָּ לְמוֹסֵרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Please, YHWH, for I [am] your servant; I [am] your servant, [the] son of your maidservant; you have loosed my bonds.

en.L: Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, truly I [am] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant; I [am] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, the son of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} maidservant; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have loosed my bonds.
en.B: Yes, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, a servant born to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant woman; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have untied the ropes that bound me.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I really am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. I have belonged to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} since I was born, because my mother was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant too. You have set me free from what held me.

decisions.choice: son of your maidservant: a servant from birth
decisions.reason: A child born to a slave woman in a household belonged to that house from birth (Genesis 17:12). The psalmist has belonged to the LORD all his life (86:16).

decisions.choice: loosed my bonds: freed me from death's ropes
decisions.reason: The bonds are the cords of death of verse 3. The LORD has untied them.

decisions.choice: servant: one who belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, 'eved for one of God's servants is "servant".

source.text: לְֽךָ־אֶ֭זְבַּח זֶ֣בַח תּוֹדָ֑ה וּבְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֶקְרָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: To you I will sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and on [the] name of YHWH I will call.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I will offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will call.
en.B: I will bring {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a thank offering and call on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by name.
en.R: I will offer {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a sacrifice to thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a sacrifice of thanksgiving: the thank offering
decisions.reason: The thank offering (todah) was a sacrifice eaten with family and friends to give thanks for rescue (Leviticus 7:12-15; 50:14; 107:22).

decisions.choice: call on the name: as in 116:4
decisions.reason: As in 116:4.

records.literal_gloss: My vows to YHWH I will pay, before, please, all his people,

en.L: My vows to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will pay, [yes], in the presence of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people,
en.B: What I promised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will carry out, with all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people looking on,
en.R: I will do what I promised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people will see me do it.

decisions.choice: the same words as verse 14
decisions.reason: The line repeats verse 14 and here leads into verse 19, which says where the vows will be kept.

decisions.choice: vows: promises made in trouble, kept with an offering
a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 19, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.literal_gloss: in [the] courts of [the] house of YHWH, in your midst, Jerusalem. Praise Yah!

en.L: in the courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in your midst, Jerusalem. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.B: in the courts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house, within you, Jerusalem. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.R: I will do it in the courtyards of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple in Jerusalem. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

decisions.choice: the courts of the house of the LORD: the temple courtyards
decisions.reason: The people gathered in the open courts around the temple building, where sacrifices were offered (84:3; 100:4).

decisions.choice: your midst, Jerusalem: the city addressed
decisions.reason: At the end the psalmist turns to speak to Jerusalem itself.

decisions.choice: Praise the LORD: Hallelu-yah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is two words: a plural command, "praise!" (hallelu), and Yah, the short form of the divine name (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It calls the gathered people to praise. Like the full name, Yah is rendered "the LORD", with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable does not address the city, to keep the sentence plain (m2).
